title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Ultrafast now available on AI Gateway
description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Ultrafast is now available on AI Gateway through Fireworks. This model can generate upwards of 1,000 tokens per second . The model has a 1M-token context window for working with large codebases and long inputs. It is available in public preview without a waitroom or session time limit. See the coding agents guide for details. Try DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 Ultrafast in the model playground . title: 与智能体语音聊天 · Cursor
description:
现在，你可以通过实时语音通话与智能体交流。直接说出你想要的更改，询问智能体正在做什么，并随着工作推进听取最新进展。

语音聊天可在智能体窗口、IDE、Web 端以及 Cursor iOS 版中使用。

当智能体处于空闲状态且聊天输入框为空时，点击标有 Start 语音聊天 的波形按钮。该按钮位于通常显示“发送”按钮的位置，旁边是用于听写的麦克风按钮。

在 iOS 上，你还可以说“Hey Siri, call Cursor”，与新的智能体发起通话，并通过锁屏界面上的实时活动静音或挂断。

语音智能体会聆听、回应，并将编程任务交给你聊天中的智能体。在该智能体运行期间，你可以继续对话：询问某个差异中改了什么、查看某次运行的进展、搜索之前与该智能体的消息和通话，或在包含多个 worker 的项目中于各个 worker 之间切换。

编程智能体也会主动开口。它会在工作过程中播报简短的进度，完成后给出简要回答，因此你通常只会听到简短的更新，而不是完整的书面回复。

语音聊天基于 Grok Voice 运行。你可以在语音设置中选择多种声音，包括 Ara、Eve、Leo、Rex 和 Sal。开启隐私

title: Ampersand from Humans& now available on AI Gateway
description: Ampersand from Humans& is now available on AI Gateway for free through November 13, 2026. Ampersand is a model for group conversations. Humans& built Ampersand on Z.ai 's open-weight GLM 5.3 and trained it with reinforcement learning in simulated group conversations that run for up to months of simulated time. Most chat models are built for one person asking a question and the model answering it. Ampersand is trained to take part in a conversation between several people. It reads every message, including the ones not addressed to it, and after each one it decides whether to reply or stay quiet. It is designed to understand individual and shared goals, help people work through disagreements, and recognize when a contribution would be useful. That can mean asking a clarifying question, sharing relevant context, or waiting while people respond to one another. For example: Sam: Heads up, I'm out Friday, driving to my sister's. Alex: Have a good trip! Maya: Let's do the launch rehearsal Friday at 10 with all three of us. Ampersand: Quick flag, Maya: Sam said he's out Friday driving to his sister's, so a Friday 10am rehearsal with all three probably won't work. Might be worth picking a different time so everyone can make it. Your application exposes these actions as caller-defined function tools . send_message delivers a contribution, while pass leaves the conversation quiet until the next human message. Your application executes both tools and records their results. Call it through the AI SDK , the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API , or a coding agent. Use humansand/ampersand-v0.1 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select humansand/ampersand-v0.1 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Ampersand in the model playground . title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
description: Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems. You define them once in code and then can update them by editing their config and redeploying. But today, agents interact with users as work evolves, and schedules need to be updated in real time. We built Vercel Schedules to allow agents and applications to create, change, or cancel one-time and recurring schedules through code, without redeploying. What are Vercel Schedules? Schedules builds on the static approach used by Vercel Cron Jobs , but are designed to let users and agents decide when work should happen while your application is still running. A schedule tells Vercel when to trigger a task and where to send it. Your application provides the code that carries out the work. You can use schedules for both static and dynamic jobs: Static schedules keep the timing in vercel.json or Build Output API configuration and sync when you deploy. You can use them to call private functions or HTTP paths, or send messages to Queue topics . Dynamic schedules let your app create and manage schedules through the JS SDK , CLI , or API as it runs. They support one-time and recurring work through Queue topics. You can also test scheduled work on Preview deployments and in custom environments before running it in Production. How Schedules works Take this example: A user could ask an agent with web access, “Tomorrow morning, summarize the top five stories on Hacker News.” The traditional solution would be storing the request and its schedule time in a database, then using a cron job to check for work that is due. With Schedules, an agent can create a schedule that records the request and when to run it, without a separate database and polling job. The example below defines an AI SDK tool that gives an agent this capability. When the task is due, Vercel uses Queues to deliver the saved request to your app. Your app provides code to read that request , check the user’s current permissions, and start the agent. The agent fetches the top five Hacker News posts with a web tool, then returns a summary for your app to save for the user. If you already build agents with fx’s JavaScript library, libfx or Pi’s agent library , you can add a similar scheduling tool. The eve agent framework uses Vercel Schedules to provide dynamic scheduling tools for production agents hosted on Vercel. Run recurring application jobs You can schedule recurring work with Vercel Schedules. Schedules can be created dynamically via the JS SDK , API , and CLI , or set up in your project’s configuration. For example, to create a job that cleans up expired records every day, you could define a schedule that invokes a private function in your chosen time zone: Vercel calls this cleanup code directly, without exposing it at a public URL. It checks that each call comes from the scheduling service, so you don’t have to add that check yourself. If your app already uses the Nitro 3 server framework, its experimental integration lets you run the recurring jobs in your existing scheduledTasks configuration as private functions. You can also try the agent task and cleanup locally with vercel dev , then test them on a Preview branch or in a custom environment before production. Use Run Schedule in your project’s Schedules tab to try either task without waiting, and see when past runs happened. Get started Vercel Schedules is now in Public Beta , and you can use it for the recurring tasks your application already runs. When a user or agent chooses when work should happen, your code can create and manage a schedule for that task. To get started, check out the Vercel Schedules skill and read the documentation . title: Vercel token scanning expands to more public sources
description: Vercel has partnered with Truffle Security to expand automated detection and revocation of publicly exposed Vercel tokens. Revoking exposed credentials helps prevent unauthorized access to your projects and unexpected costs from unauthorized use of services such as Vercel Sandbox and Vercel AI Gateway . If your token is revoked, you’ll receive an email from us explaining why. Truffle Security reports tokens exposed in public sources including GitHub, GitLab, Docker, npm, PyPI, Hugging Face, Android APKs, and Firefox Add-ons. Vercel has revoked hundreds of tokens reported by Truffle Security. A separate Vercel scanner now checks each new monthly Common Crawl dataset of public web pages and automatically revokes any exposed Vercel tokens it finds. Learn more about creating tokens, setting their scopes, and managing them in the access token documentation . Read more
